- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.4) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 10+ day forecasts, model tends to underestimate if sentiment is weak or mixed — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward historical average.
